Question B-005-008-004.

Why the correct answer is right: Reducing power from 200 W to 20 W is a factor of 10 decrease, which is 10 dB down. Starting at 10 dB over S9, subtracting 10 dB lands at S9.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "S9 plus 3 dB": That would be only 7 dB below the original reading, not the full 10 dB caused by a ten-to-one power reduction.
- sourceIndex 2: "S9 minus 10 dB": This subtracts 20 dB from the starting point of 10 dB over S9. The power change supplies a 10 dB reduction, not 20 dB.
- sourceIndex 3: "S9 plus 5 dB": Five dB over S9 would leave half of the original dB margin; the 200 W to 20 W change removes all 10 dB over S9.
